✎ If you have zero dollars in your bank account, you can still start a business and become a successful entrepreneur. John Paul DeJoria was completely broke and living out of his car with only $700 to his name when he started. He partnered with a friend to sell hair products door-to-door to local salons because he could not afford advertising. Today, his company makes over a billion dollars a year because he decided to start before he felt ready. Your time, hustle, and consistency are the most important tools you need to solve expensive problems and create real financial freedom today.

snippet.title: The Genius Business Model of Buy Now Pay Later
snippet.description:
If you’ve bought anything online in the last couple of years, you’ve probably noticed some new payment option when getting to the checkout page of many online retailers Companies like Affirm, Afterpay, and Klarna have all started offering buy now pay later services that allow users to pay for their purchases over a series of instatement rather than paying up front and in full at checkout. The rise of this new payment form represents a major shift in the payments industry, offering consumers increased flexibility in managing their finances while avoiding the often times aggressive fees from credit cards. But with so much attention being paid to the buy now pay later market, I figured we should take a look at the underlying business model to get a better understanding of the market overall and determine for ourselves whether the hype is truly justified.

snippet.description:
Business strategy, business model, entrepreneurship, and one of the smartest distribution systems ever built. Discover how a fleet of red vans helped create a multi-billion-dollar company without relying on traditional retail stores.

Most companies wait for customers to walk through the door. This company built an empire by driving directly to them.

This is the remarkable business story behind Snap-on's mobile retail strategy—and why competitors still struggle to copy it.

🚀 Subscribe to The Business Case:

Turn on notifications so you never miss powerful business documentaries, founder stories, corporate strategy, branding, and the hidden decisions behind the world's most successful companies.

Most companies invest millions in opening better stores.

Snap-on built one of the world's most successful retail systems by asking a completely different question:

What if the store came to the customer instead?

In this documentary, you'll discover how a simple idea transformed a premium tool manufacturer into a company worth billions—without depending on traditional retail locations.

We'll explore the invention of the interchangeable socket system, the psychology behind the famous green felt demonstrations, the surprising financing model developed during the Great Depression, and the fleet of mobile stores that still visits professional mechanics every week.

You'll also learn why a single Snap-on franchise van can generate hundreds of thousands of dollars in annual revenue, why trust became the company's greatest competitive advantage, and why its business model has remained incredibly difficult to copy for more than a century.

This isn't just the story of premium tools.

It's the story of one of the smartest distribution systems ever created.

In this video you'll learn:

✔ How Snap-on invented a revolutionary interchangeable socket system

✔ Why selling directly inside repair shops changed the entire industry

✔ The surprising psychology behind the famous green felt demonstration

✔ How the Great Depression helped shape Snap-on's financing strategy

✔ Why weekly customer visits became the company's greatest competitive advantage

✔ How one mobile showroom can generate extraordinary annual revenue

✔ Why competitors can copy the products—but not the system

✔ The real reason Snap-on has remained one of the world's most respected professional tool brands

Great businesses don't always win because they build better products.

Sometimes they win because they build better systems.

Snap-on proved that the greatest competitive advantage isn't always found inside the product itself.

Sometimes it's found in the way that product reaches the customer.

32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex
